If X<=Y coordinatewise is an ordered coupling of binary-product laws mu and nu on a countable edge set E, then every increasing event A supported on a finite F satisfies 0<=nu(A)-mu(A)<=sum_{e in F}(nu(omega_e=1)-mu(omega_e=1)). A difference of event indicators requires at least one support coordinate to differ; use a union bound, not independence. Equal one-edge marginals of ordered laws force equality of the laws.

relation.rationale: The explicit alpha^L path gap shows why the criterion requires a positive infinite-volume gap on fixed finite support, rather than positivity separately in every outer volume.

from_statement_quoted: Unreviewed campaign concept; independent referee w461 pending. On a path with L>=1 edges, q>1 and 0<p<1, put alpha=p/[p+q*(1-p)]. Free random-cluster edges are iid Bernoulli(alpha). Wiring the two endpoints tilts that law by 1+(q-1)*1_{all edges open}. Therefore the wired minus free marginal gap at each edge is (q-1)*(1-alpha)*alpha^L/[1+(q-1)*alpha^L], positive at every finite L and tending to zero. For q=3,p=1/2 it is 1/4 at L=1 and 1/172 at L=4. Finite-size positivity alone cannot establish an infinite-volume gap. This d=1 example refutes the inference, not C0048 for d>=3.

from_statement_quoted: Unreviewed campaign concept; independent referee w461 pending. This is an abstract finite-state example, not a claimed nearest-neighbor Potts model.
